findings.location: Definition, first paragraph: graph distance d_Γ and its use in the Gaussian submodel
findings.evidence: The finite undirected graph is not required to be connected, but d_Γ is only named as graph distance. The later condition A_xy=0 when d_Γ(x,y)>1 is undefined for disconnected pairs. Define extended shortest-path distance with value +∞, or restrict the graph to be connected.

findings.location: Definition, positive heavy-scalar Gaussian submodel paragraph: operator norm, P_E, and J(ℓ)
findings.evidence: The item uses ‖A‖ and calls P_E an orthogonal spectral projection without specifying the Euclidean structure or complexification, and does not state how the spectral-measure construction in its QFT-unit supplier applies to the real matrix A; it also does not type J as a map from retained-coordinate space. The exact inner product, A_ℂ, PVM use, and source-map domain are needed to make these data precise.

findings.location: Definition, positive heavy-scalar Gaussian submodel paragraph: ν_H
findings.evidence: The general model record leaves ν_H as any specified Borel probability, and the Gaussian submodel adds A and K but never requires ν_H to be a centered Gaussian probability with covariance K⁻¹. That measure law is needed to define the advertised Gaussian submodel and match its stated kernel.

The integral exponent requires dimensionless S_UV. The definition calls S_UV a real Borel ultraviolet action but does not state that it is normalized as the physical action divided by ℏ; natural-unit notation alone does not identify that normalization.

findings.location: Definition, final paragraph on the one-particle-irreducible effective action
findings.evidence: The paragraph identifies the 1PI action only as a Legendre transform of a connected source-generating functional. It gives no source and field spaces, pairing, sign convention, or differentiability/invertibility conditions defining that transform. Supply an exact convention or remove the aside.
